plain.li: [fire] Move up, there's room on this side of the fire.
[fire,cold] Get closer to the fire, the night's turned cold.
[fire,lowtech] We'll want a proper hearth before long, but this will do tonight.
[!fire] No fire tonight, but we're all here, and that's the main thing.
[rain] Rain on the first night, of all nights.
[snow] Snow on our first night here, that's one to tell later.
[clear,night] Look at the stars, the same ones as ever, and they still look new from here.
[clear] A clear sky for the first night, I'll take that as a good sign.
[winter] Whoever picked winter for this owes us all a warm bed.
[summer] At least the nights are warm for now.
[fall] We'll want the stores in before the frost.
[spring] Spring's a good time to start anything, even a colony.
[!newcomer] I keep reaching for things that are back at the old place.
[!newcomer] Funny, I already miss the noise of the old place.
[!newcomer] The old place had its faults, but I knew where everything was.
[newcomer] A few days ago I'd never heard of this place.
[newcomer] So this is what we answered the call for.
[newcomer] I came a long way for this, and I'm not sorry.
[old] I'm too old to be starting over, and here I am, starting over.
[teen] I'm going to remember tonight for the rest of my life.
[child,fire] Can we sleep by the fire tonight?
[child,night] It's very dark out there.
[hurt] I'll be more use tomorrow, I promise.
[small] Just us, then, and a lot of empty land.
[large] There are more of us than I expected, which is good news.
[highmood] I don't think I've ever felt this hopeful.
[lowmood] Ask me tomorrow whether this was a good idea.
[tribal] The ground here sleeps differently, I can feel it.
[medieval] We'll need a well, a wall and a roof, in that order.
[industrial] Tomorrow I'll take stock of everything we brought.
[spacer] Strange to sleep on ground we haven't surveyed yet.
[speaker] We start at first light, so get some sleep tonight.
[speaker,!newcomer] We didn't come out here to be comfortable, we came to build something.
[speaker,newcomer] Some of us are strangers tonight, and that won't last long.
[speaker] Whatever this place becomes, tonight is where it started.
[speaker,fire] Look into the fire a moment, all of you, and remember tonight.
[speaker,tribal] The spirits of this land don't know us yet, so let's give them something good to see.
[speaker,medieval] We have a name, a patch of ground and each other, and that's charter enough for tonight.
[speaker,industrial] First thing tomorrow, we mark out where everything goes.
[speaker,spacer] Tomorrow we survey, tonight we rest.

blunt.li: Eat, sleep, and we'll argue about walls in the morning.

cheerful.li: Our own place, our own sky, and our own mistakes to make!

gloomy.li: Every new place looks kind on the first night.

cold.li: Sleep in shifts, we don't know who else is out there.

plain.li: [leave] We'll send word the day we have a roof over us.
[leave] The road's long, so let's not stand about.
[leave] One more look, and then I'm not looking back.
[leave] I've packed everything I own, and it still doesn't feel like enough.
[leave,old] I didn't think I'd be setting out again at my age.
[leave,child] Is it far?
[leave,teen] I can't believe we're really going.
[leave,winter] Cold day for a long road.
[leave,rain] Wet start, but it's a start.
[leave,morning] An early start, and a long way to go.
[leave,tribal] The land ahead doesn't know us yet, but it will.
[leave,medieval] We go with the council's blessing, which will have to do for a roof tonight.
[leave,industrial] Everything's loaded, checked, and checked again.
[leave,spacer] Route plotted and supplies logged, so there's no reason to wait.
[seeoff] Mind how you go, the road won't mind it for you.
[seeoff] Don't forget us once you're settled.
[seeoff] Supper's going to be quiet tonight.
[seeoff] Take care of each other out there.
[seeoff] Go well, all of you.
[seeoff,!tribal] Write when you get there, or send someone with the news.
[seeoff,child] When can I come and see it?
[seeoff,old] I'm too old for that road, but I'm glad you're not.
[seeoff,lowtech] Walk safe, and may the land be kind to you.
[seeoff,winter] Keep your feet dry and your fires lit.
[seeoff,rain] You picked a wet day for it.

cheerful.li: [leave] New place, new start, let's go!
[seeoff] Go on, and make us jealous.

gloomy.li: [leave] I hope we're not making a mistake.

cold.li: [leave] We have what we need, so let's move.
[seeoff] Go, then, and do it properly.

plain.li: I'll never remember all the new names by tomorrow.
Somebody pass the bread down to the far end.
It's a full table tonight, and that's how I like it.
I keep looking up and seeing faces I don't know yet.
[eating] This tastes better with more people round it.
Tomorrow we'll sort out who sleeps where, tonight we eat.
Two councils' worth of opinions at one table, this should be lively.
I'll trade you stories of the old place for stories of this one.
[child] There are so many people at supper now.
[old] I like a table this full.
[winter] It's good to have more of us for the winter.
[summer] Long evenings ahead, and plenty of time to get to know each other.
[lowtech] More mouths and more hands, and that's a fair trade.
[speaker] There's a place at this table for every one of you, tonight and after.
[speaker] Sit anywhere, there's no old side and new side at this table.
[speaker] Tonight we eat, and tomorrow we work the rest out together.

cheerful.li: A full table and a full pot, what more could anyone want?

gloomy.li: It'll take more than one supper to make one colony of us.

plain.li: [speaker] To {OLD}, which we'll remember, and to {PLACE}, which is all of ours now.
[speaker] Raise your cups to the people of {OLD}, and welcome home.
[speaker] Tonight {PLACE} grows, and it's the better for it.
[speaker] To everyone who came here from {OLD}: sit down, eat, and stay.
[speaker] {OLD} lives on at this table, in every one of you.
[speaker,lowtech] The fires of {OLD} and {PLACE} burn as one from tonight.
[speaker,tribal] Two bands, one fire, and may the spirits see it.
[speaker,medieval] Let it be said that on this night {OLD} and {PLACE} became one.
[speaker,industrial] Two settlements, one table, one council, so welcome, all of you.
[speaker,spacer] Two colonies on one roster from tonight, and welcome to {PLACE}.
[speaker,winter] Come in from the cold, people of {OLD}, to the warmest table we have.
[speaker] There are no guests at this table tonight, only the people of {PLACE}.

warm.li: [speaker] I've looked forward to this supper, so welcome, all of you.

cheerful.li: [speaker] To {OLD} and {PLACE}, and to the longest table we've ever needed!

cold.li: [speaker] You are of {PLACE} now, and we expect the best of you.

plain.li: [speaker] Let's go round the table, and everyone gets their say.
[speaker] Nobody is being sent anywhere tonight, we're only deciding.
[speaker] Think of the ones who would stay, and whether they want this.
If they want to run it themselves, maybe they've earned it.
I'd want to know who would lead it before I vote.
Either way the place stays standing, it just stops being ours to run.
I'd rather hand it over than leave it to fall down.
[tribal] The elders would say a fire must have its keepers.
[medieval] A free town with our own people in it would make a good neighbor.
[industrial] The numbers say it can stand on its own, if the people want it.
[spacer] The systems can run without us, the question is whether the people should.
[old] At my age you don't rush a choice like this.
[lowmood] I'm not ready to vote on this, but I suppose I have to.
[trusting] If the council thinks it's time, I'm listening.
[doubtful] I want to hear how this is good for the ones who stay, not just the rest of us.

warm.li: Whatever happens, I'd like us to part as friends.

blunt.li: Vote, and stop talking in circles.

cheerful.li: Our own people running their own town, I like the sound of that.

gloomy.li: It feels like the end of something, however we vote.

cold.li: Feelings aside, can it stand on its own or not?

plain.li: [speaker] We'll keep the walls up and the gate open, for you most of all.
[speaker] Those of you who go, go knowing this place stands behind you.
[speaker] I'll lead it as well as I know how.
[speaker,tribal] The fire will be kept, and the stories with it.
[speaker,medieval] This hall has a new master and the same old roof.
[speaker,industrial] The township opens for business tomorrow morning.
[speaker,spacer] The new administration is in place, and the channel to you stays open.
This is the last time we'll all stand here as one colony.
Look around, it'll be a while before we're all in one place again.
Whatever we're called after today, we started out together.
[lowtech] The old ones will tell this day to the young ones, you'll see.
[!tribal] Somebody should be writing this down.
[old] I never thought I'd see this place stand on its own.
[child] Will we still see each other?
[teen] So it's a town now?

warm.li: We're still the same people, whatever we call it now.

cheerful.li: A town of our own people, imagine that.

gloomy.li: Tomorrow I'll keep looking for faces that aren't here.

plain.li: Take good care of it, it took a lot of work.
I know you'll do better with it than we would have.
Don't let anyone tell you how we'd have done it.
[tribal] Keep the totem where the fire can see it.
[medieval] The keys, and the charter, and every promise in it.
[industrial] Here are the papers, all signed, and the keys.
[spacer] Access transferred, and every code is yours.

warm.li: Be good to it, and to them.

plain.li: I'll keep it safe, and the people with it.
It's heavier than it looks.
I won't let you down.
[tribal] The totem stays, and so does the fire.
[medieval] I'll have the charter read out on this day every year.
[industrial] Signed and received, and thank you for everything.
[spacer] Codes accepted, and you'll always have a way back in.
[old] I'm old for this, but I'll manage.

warm.li: Thank you for trusting me with all of it.

plain.li: [going] I'll think of you every time I sit down to eat.
[going] Don't forget me while I'm gone.
[going] I'll send word from the road.
[going] I'll come back to visit, I promise.
[going,old] At my age every goodbye feels like the last one.
[going,child] Will you come and see me?
[staying] Send word, or I'll come and find you.
[staying] It won't feel right, you not being here.
[staying] I'll look after things here, don't worry.
[staying] Come back when you can, this town owes you that.
[staying,old] Don't leave it too long before you visit, I'm not getting younger.
[staying,child] Will you come back?
[staying] Take care of yourself out there.

cheerful.li: [going] I'll be back to brag about the new place, you'll see.
[staying] Go on, have an adventure for both of us.

plain.li: I keep thinking about the day we set out for {LABEL}.
Remember the first morning at {LABEL}, everyone wondering where to start?
[first] We've never really talked about founding {LABEL}, have we?
[friends] I'm glad you were one of the founders of {LABEL}.
[lowtech] Remember marking out where the first walls of {LABEL} would go?
[!lowtech] Remember sorting the kit at {LABEL}, working out what we'd forgotten?
[old] I didn't think I had another fresh start in me, and then came {LABEL}.
Sometimes I try to see {LABEL} the way it looked on the first day.

warm.li: Founding {LABEL} with you is one of the best things I've done.

blunt.li: We built {LABEL}, nobody handed it to us.

cheerful.li: {LABEL} was a wild idea, and it worked!

gloomy.li: I still can't decide if founding {LABEL} was brave or foolish.

cold.li: Founding {LABEL} was the sound decision, whatever anyone says.

plain.li: I remember the quiet more than anything.
We argued about everything at the start.
I remember being so tired.
[lowtech] The first fire, and everyone too tired to talk.
[!lowtech] I remember counting the supplies every night.
I'd do it again, I think.
[first] I didn't know you thought about it too.
We had more hope than sense back then.

warm.li: It was worth it, all of it, because you were there.

blunt.li: We did the work, that's what I remember.

cheerful.li: Best thing any of us ever did.

gloomy.li: I remember being sure it would fail.

plain.li: Here's to the founders of {LABEL}.
We should tell the newer ones about it some time.
It was a good start, whatever came after.
Let's not leave it so long before we talk about it again.
I'm glad we did it.

gloomy.li: Funny how long ago it feels.
